stem: The student wants to emphasize a difference in the depths at which the two jellyfish species live. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Over three years, marine biologist Ines Okafor surveyed two jellyfish species off the coast of Namibia.
• The violet sail jelly lives mostly in the top 10 meters of the water.
• The ember jelly typically lives between 400 and 600 meters below the surface.
• Both species feed on small crustaceans.
choices: Over three years, marine biologist Ines Okafor surveyed two jellyfish species, the violet sail jelly and the ember jelly, off Namibia.
The violet sail jelly and the ember jelly, both found off the coast of Namibia, feed on small crustaceans.
The violet sail jelly lives in the top 10 meters of water, whereas the ember jelly lives 400 to 600 meters down.
The ember jelly, which feeds on small crustaceans, typically lives between 400 and 600 meters below the surface.
explanation: The goal asks about depth, so you need both species and both depths in the same sentence. Choice C gives the violet sail jelly's depth (top 10 meters) and the ember jelly's depth (400 to 600 meters), and 'whereas' says outright that they differ.

A.why: You picked a choice that names both species but never says how they differ. Naming both items without comparing them is the trap this question type is built around. This choice says nothing about depth.

B.why: You picked a choice about something the two species share, their diet. The goal asks for a difference, and a similarity can't show one.

D.why: You picked a choice that gives only the ember jelly's depth. Without the violet sail jelly's depth, you have nothing to compare it to.

stem: The student wants to emphasize a difference in how quickly muscle soreness subsided after the two methods. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Sports scientists compared two cooldown methods used by college sprinters after hard workouts.
• In cold-water immersion, sprinters sit in 10°C water for 12 minutes.
• In active recovery, sprinters jog lightly for 12 minutes.
• After cold-water immersion, muscle soreness subsided in about 24 hours.
• After active recovery, muscle soreness subsided in about 48 hours.
choices: Muscle soreness subsided in about 24 hours after cold-water immersion but took about 48 hours after active recovery.
Cold-water immersion has sprinters sit in 10°C water for 12 minutes, while active recovery has them jog lightly.
Cold-water immersion and active recovery each last 12 minutes when they are used by college sprinters.
Unlike active recovery, cold-water immersion prevented any muscle soreness among the college sprinters.
explanation: The goal limits you to one attribute: how quickly soreness went away. Choice A gives both methods' times (24 hours and 48 hours), and 'but' marks the contrast.

B.why: You picked a real contrast on the wrong attribute. This choice compares what each method involves, but the goal asked about how quickly soreness subsided.

C.why: You picked a choice that gives something the two methods share, their 12-minute length. A shared feature can't emphasize a difference.

D.why: You picked a choice that claims more than the notes support. The notes say soreness subsided in about 24 hours after cold-water immersion. They never say soreness was prevented.

stem: The student wants to emphasize how the two lutes differ in their number of strings. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• A conservatory museum in Padua, Italy, holds two eighteenth-century lutes.
• The older lute, built around 1715, has 11 strings.
• The newer lute, built around 1760, has 24 strings.
• Both lutes have bodies made of thin maple ribs.
• Musicologist Teodora Vance catalogued the pair in 2019.
choices: Musicologist Teodora Vance catalogued two eighteenth-century lutes held by a conservatory museum in Padua.
Both of the eighteenth-century lutes in the Padua museum have bodies made of thin maple ribs.
One of the museum's lutes was built around 1715, while the other was built some 45 years later.
The lute built around 1715 has 11 strings, while the one built around 1760 has more than twice as many.

A.why: You picked a choice that mentions both lutes but never compares them. It says nothing about strings at all.

B.why: You picked a similarity, the maple bodies, when the goal asked for a difference.

C.why: You picked a contrast on the wrong attribute. The two lutes do differ in age, but the goal asked about their number of strings.

stem: The student wants to contrast the drawbacks of the two coatings. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Engineers tested two coatings meant to protect steel bridge cables from corrosion.
• Zinc coating is inexpensive to apply.
• Zinc coating wears away within about 15 years in salty coastal air.
• Epoxy coating resists salty coastal air for more than 40 years.
• Epoxy coating can crack when cables flex in freezing weather.
choices: Zinc coating is inexpensive to apply, while epoxy coating resists salty coastal air for more than 40 years.
Zinc coating wears away within about 15 years in salty air, while epoxy coating can crack in freezing weather.
Engineers tested zinc and epoxy, two coatings meant to protect steel bridge cables from corrosion.
Epoxy coating can crack when cables flex in freezing weather, so it should never be used on northern bridges.
explanation: The goal limits you to drawbacks. Choice B gives one weakness for each coating: zinc wears away within about 15 years, and epoxy can crack in freezing weather. 'While' sets the two side by side.

A.why: You picked a contrast on the wrong attribute. Low cost and long life in salty air are advantages, but the goal asked for drawbacks.

C.why: You picked a choice that names both coatings but gives neither one's drawback, so it contrasts nothing.

D.why: You picked a choice that turns one note into a recommendation the notes never make. It also covers only epoxy, so there is nothing to contrast it with.

stem: The student wants to emphasize a difference in union membership between the two industries. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Economist Rafael Duarte studied union membership in two industries in 2022.
• In trucking, 9% of workers belonged to a union.
• In public transit, 58% of workers belonged to a union.
• Workers in both industries averaged about 42 hours of work per week.
• Duarte's figures came from a national labor survey.
choices: Using data from a national labor survey, Duarte studied union membership among trucking and public transit workers.
Trucking workers and public transit workers both averaged about 42 hours of work per week in 2022.
In 2022, 58% of public transit workers belonged to a union, compared with just 9% of trucking workers.
In 2022, trucking workers were far more likely than public transit workers to belong to a union.
explanation: Choice C names both industries and gives both union membership rates. 'Compared with just' makes the gap between 58% and 9% explicit.

A.why: You picked a choice that names both industries and the topic but never gives the rates. It doesn't show any difference.

B.why: You picked something the two industries share, their weekly hours. The goal asked for a difference, and in union membership specifically.

D.why: You picked a choice that gets the comparison backwards. The notes give trucking 9% and public transit 58%, so public transit workers were the ones more likely to belong to a union.

stem: The student wants to emphasize a difference in where ink is held on the printing surface in the two methods. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Relief printing and intaglio are two major families of printmaking.
• Woodcut is a common type of relief printing.
• In relief printing, the artist carves away the areas that will not print, and ink sits on the raised surfaces that remain.
• Etching is a common type of intaglio.
• In intaglio, ink is held in lines cut or etched below the plate's surface.
• Relief prints can be pressed by hand, while intaglio prints require a heavy press.
choices: Relief printing and intaglio, which include woodcut and etching, are two major families of printmaking.
In relief printing, ink sits on raised surfaces, whereas in intaglio it is held in lines below the plate's surface.
Relief prints can be pressed by hand, whereas intaglio prints require the force of a heavy press.
In relief printing, ink is held below the plate's surface, whereas in intaglio it sits on raised areas.
explanation: The goal limits you to one attribute: where the ink is held. Choice B names both methods and uses 'whereas' to set their different answers side by side: on raised surfaces for relief printing, and below the surface for intaglio.

A.why: You picked a choice that names both methods but never says how they differ. Listing two things side by side does not contrast them.

C.why: This choice does contrast the two methods, but it compares how they are pressed, not where the ink is held. Check which attribute the goal asks about.

D.why: This choice reverses the notes. Relief printing holds ink on raised surfaces, and intaglio holds it below the surface.

stem: The student wants to emphasize a difference in how much nitrogen the two cover crops add to the soil. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Cover crops are planted between cash-crop seasons to protect and enrich farm soil.
• Crimson clover is a legume often used as a cover crop.
• Crimson clover can add about 100 pounds of nitrogen per acre to the soil.
• Cereal rye is a grass often used as a cover crop.
• Cereal rye adds little nitrogen to the soil, but its dense roots help prevent erosion.
• Cereal rye survives colder winters than crimson clover does.
choices: Cereal rye survives colder winters than crimson clover does, so it suits farms in colder regions.
Crimson clover and cereal rye are both cover crops planted between cash-crop seasons.
Because crimson clover adds nitrogen to the soil, it is the better cover crop for every farm.
Crimson clover can add about 100 pounds of nitrogen per acre to the soil, while cereal rye adds little.
explanation: The goal asks for a difference in nitrogen. Choice D gives each crop's nitrogen contribution, about 100 pounds per acre for clover and little for rye, and uses 'while' to mark the contrast.

A.why: This choice compares the crops on winter hardiness instead of nitrogen. It is a real difference, but not the one the goal names.

B.why: This choice names both crops but points out something they share. The goal asked for a difference.

C.why: The notes never say that clover is better for every farm. Rye's erosion control could matter more on some farms, so this choice claims more than the notes support.

stem: The student wants to contrast how much vitamin C the two cooking methods preserved. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Vitamin C is a nutrient that can be lost when vegetables are cooked.
• A team of food scientists measured vitamin C in broccoli cooked two ways.
• Steamed broccoli kept about 90 percent of its original vitamin C.
• Boiled broccoli kept about 50 percent of its original vitamin C.
• Vitamin C dissolves in water, which may explain the larger loss from boiling.
choices: Steamed broccoli kept about 90 percent of its vitamin C, but boiled broccoli kept only about 50 percent.
Food scientists measured vitamin C in broccoli that had been steamed and in broccoli that had been boiled.
Boiled broccoli kept about 50 percent of its vitamin C, likely because the vitamin dissolves in water.
Steamed broccoli and boiled broccoli each kept a similar share of their vitamin C, about 70 percent.
explanation: To contrast the two methods, you need both percentages joined by a word that signals contrast. Choice A gives 90 percent for steaming and 50 percent for boiling, and links them with 'but... only.'

B.why: This choice names both cooking methods but describes only what the study did. It never says how the results differed.

C.why: This choice gives a figure for boiling only, so there is nothing to contrast it with. It also turns toward explaining the loss instead of comparing the methods.

D.why: The notes report clearly different amounts, 90 percent and 50 percent, not a similar 70 percent for both.

stem: The student wants to contrast a drawback of linen with a drawback of wool. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• In eighteenth-century Europe, linen and wool were the most common fabrics for everyday clothing.

• Wool, made from sheep's fleece, was warm and held dye well.
• A drawback of wool was that it shrank when washed in hot water.
• In many rural households, both fibers were spun at home.
choices: Linen was cool and absorbent, whereas wool was warm and held dye well.
Both linen and wool were spun at home in many rural European households.
Linen wrinkled easily, whereas wool tended to shrink in hot water.
Linen shrank in hot water, whereas wool tended to wrinkle easily.
explanation: The goal limits you to drawbacks. Choice C gives the drawback of each fabric, wrinkling for linen and shrinking for wool, and uses 'whereas' to contrast them.

A.why: This choice is set up as a contrast, but it compares the fabrics' advantages. The goal asked for drawbacks.

B.why: This choice describes something the two fibers share. It neither contrasts them nor mentions a drawback.

D.why: This choice swaps the drawbacks. According to the notes, linen wrinkled and wool shrank.

stem: The student wants to emphasize the difference in average weekly hours worked by the two groups. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

• In 2023, an economist surveyed workers in two sectors of a regional economy.
• The survey included 600 warehouse workers and 600 retail workers.
• Warehouse workers averaged 44 hours of work per week.
• Retail workers averaged 31 hours of work per week.
• Retail workers were more likely than warehouse workers to hold a second job (38 percent vs. 12 percent).
choices: Retail workers were more likely than warehouse workers to hold a second job, 38 percent to 12 percent.
Warehouse workers averaged 44 hours of work per week, whereas retail workers averaged only 31.
The economist surveyed 600 warehouse workers and 600 retail workers about their weekly hours.
Warehouse workers averaged 44 hours of work per week, so they earned more than retail workers.
explanation: The goal names the attribute: average weekly hours. Choice B gives both groups' averages, 44 and 31, and uses 'whereas... only' to stress the gap.

A.why: This choice does contrast the two groups, but on holding a second job, not on weekly hours. That is the wrong attribute.

C.why: This choice names both groups and the topic of hours, but it describes only the survey. It never says how the groups' hours differed.

D.why: The notes say nothing about earnings. Working more hours does not by itself show that warehouse workers earned more.
